summary.headline: Bluspring Q1 FY27 revenue ex-foundit up 20% YoY to INR930 crores; EBITDA INR35 crores (+48% YoY), margin 3.8%, guidance of INR4,700 crores revenue reiterated.
summary.overview: Ex-foundit revenue rose 20% YoY and 10% QoQ to INR930 crores, with EBITDA of INR35 crores (+48% YoY, flat QoQ) and PAT of INR16 crores (+47% YoY). STEAG Energy Services was consolidated from May 21, 2026, and contributed INR76 crores to the Smart Infra, Energy and Engineering segment. Management reiterated FY27 guidance (ex-investments) of over INR4,700 crores revenue, over INR200 crores EBITDA and over INR100 crores PAT, and said the LSG Sky Chefs acquisition (INR166 crores) is set to close within weeks. foundit remained loss-making, with a quarterly EBITDA loss of about INR14 crores.

segments.name: Facility and food services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR520 crores (+9% YoY, flat QoQ) and EBITDA INR24 crores (+25% YoY, -3% QoQ); margin 4.6% vs 4.0% a year ago. About 40 new clients added with ACV of about INR89 crores.

segments.name: Security services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR185-187 crores (+24-25% YoY, +10% QoQ) and EBITDA INR5 crores (+37-43% YoY, -12% QoQ); margin 2.8%. Headcount crossed 24,900 after about 900 net adds; 37 new clients with ACV of INR43 crores.

segments.name: Smart Infra, Energy and Engineering (formerly Telecom and Industrial)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR223-229 crores (+47% YoY, +42% QoQ), with STEAG contributing INR76 crores; EBITDA INR21 crores (+80% YoY); margin about 9.2-9.3% vs 8.2%. Telecom was muted on seasonality.

segments.name: foundit
segments.commentary: Revenue INR19 crores with bookings of INR25 crores; EBITDA loss about INR14 crores; cost base about INR32-33 crores. Management guides FY27 cash burn of INR30-35 crores (INR35-40 crores in a later answer) and breakeven by Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ex-investments: revenue over INR4,700 crores (about 42% YoY), EBITDA over INR200 crores (about 65% YoY), PAT over INR100 crores (about 50% YoY).
Exit FY27 with EBITDA margin above 5%; ROE to rise from about 7% in FY26 to about 13% in FY27. ROE target of 20% and margin of 5.5-6% pulled forward to FY29 from FY30.
STEAG FY27 revenue close to INR1,000 crores at 7-8% EBITDA margin; STEAG's four large contracts add over INR5,100-5,200 crores over five years.
Organic revenue growth guided at 15-16% for FY27.
Net debt/EBITDA below 1x by year-end; acquisition debt about INR150 crores at year-end with organic net debt about zero, though average organic debt of INR150-175 crores.
Effective tax rate guided at about 22%. Working capital days guided to about 45 including STEAG and LSG.
LSG Sky Chefs: about INR110 crores pro forma FY26 revenue, high-teen EBITDA margin, INR125 crores debt to fund; closing in next couple of weeks.
capex_capacity: STEAG acquisition closed May 21, 2026; three of four large contracts live since July 1, the fourth from early August.
LSG India Bengaluru in-flight catering kitchen: concession to operate until 2039; INR112 crores FY26 revenue; debt-free with INR57 crores cash.
Workforce 97,000 at Q1 end, up 3,300 QoQ; crossed about 100,000 in July.
Security headcount above 24,900 after about 900 net adds in the quarter.
demand_pricing: Client vendor consolidation and outsourcing trends cited; management says about two-thirds of facility management is still in-house.
Customer retention about 95%; new business adds about 10% a year; about 4-5% of business lost to competition each year.
STEAG's O&M work is about 90% thermal; management cites about 250 GW of peak demand and STEAG's 14-16 GW portfolio.
Security and FM described as commoditised; STEAG and Hofincons differentiated on German technical pedigree, with plant availability improved from 83-84% to 93-94% for clients.
Telecom softness in Q1, with early July rollout signs from large players; management expects better H2 telecom.
Food margins range 5-10% by segment; aviation catering at the high end. LPG price increases pressured food margins.
Subcontracting cost rose to about INR108 crores from INR78 crores QoQ, mainly from telecom and STEAG.

financial_highlights.value: INR307 crores / INR135 crores / INR172 crores

qa_highlights.question: How will management run the three divisions over the next two years, and what is the addressable market for STEAG-type contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Each of the three businesses has its own leadership team and board-set growth targets. Management cites vendor consolidation, outsourcing (about two-thirds of FM still in-house) and GST/Labour Code formalisation. STEAG's large contracts are end-to-end outcome-based O&M, combining STEAG, Hofincons and the FM team.

qa_highlights.question: What is the foundit path to breakeven and how much more funding is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets Q4 FY27 breakeven. Cost base is about INR32-33 crores and will not rise. FY27 cash burn guided at INR35-40 crores in one answer, versus INR30-35 crores in the prepared remarks. Breakeven needs quarterly sales above INR35-40 crores, with revenue recognised from subscriptions over a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did foundit sales of about INR10 crores more over two quarters not show up in revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said B2B subscription revenue is deferred and recognised as service is consumed, with sales-to-revenue ratio of about 15-18%. Leakage fell from about 40% to about 20%. Revenue rose from INR17-18 crores to INR19 crores, with INR21 crores expected next and INR22-23 crores in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise to INR108 crores from INR78 crores QoQ, and what is the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: The jump is mainly subcontracting in telecom and STEAG. The CFO said the new base should hold for the next 2-3 quarters given STEAG.

qa_highlights.question: What are the STEAG contract economics: FY27 revenue, margin and five-year sustainability after the initial term?
qa_highlights.answer: STEAG FY27 revenue is close to INR1,000 crores at 7-8% EBITDA margin, with consolidation from May 21. Contracts run five years with extension options. Plant availability improved from 83-84% to 93-94% for clients, which management cites as the basis for renewal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook and are there deposits for large deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic working capital days are about 37. Including STEAG and the large contracts, management guided about 45 days, with a possible rise of about eight days before it settles. Power contracts need non-funded bank guarantees, not cash deposits.

qa_highlights.question: How do long-term margin and ROE targets change after the acquisitions, and what is the ELI scheme impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The 20% ROE and 5.5-6% EBITDA margin targets are kept but pulled forward from FY30 to mostly FY29. Management has seen no substantial ELI scheme benefit so far.

risks_watch: foundit: sustained losses, a cash burn guide that moved from INR30-35 crores to INR35-40 crores, and breakeven by Q4 FY27 that depends on sales converting to revenue.
Subcontracting cost jump (INR78 crores to INR108 crores QoQ) and whether it stays at this run rate; margin dilution from STEAG and telecom.
Working capital days guided to rise to about 45 with STEAG and LSG, versus 37 today; cash conversion and bank guarantee requirements on large contracts.
Security margins below 3% (2.8% in Q1) with ECL-driven drop; management's 4-4.5% target depends on catching up in Q2 and Q3.
Telecom softness in Q1; recovery depends on capex revival from Q2 and H2 FY27 telecom orders.
Debt: net debt INR172 crores, acquisition debt about INR150 crores at year end, and LSG INR125 crores debt funding due within weeks.
Execution and renewal of STEAG's four large five-year contracts, and the fourth contract starting from early August.
key_quotes: This is a high entry barrier, high margin, and highly regulated business with multi -year contractual cash flows.
We feel that we have a phenomenal opportunity.

So, we are hopeful that the second half of the year including quarter 2 for telecom should be better, and which means telecom as a whole for our portfolio should do better year-on-year from an overall revenue and EBITDA standpoint.
We expect the EBITDA burn for the financial year to be in the range of INR30 crores to INR35 crores.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, the STEAG order book and FY27 guidance, which management repeated and in places said it would reach a year early. More cautious on foundit, where it conceded the sales-to-revenue gap and shifted the cash burn guidance, and on Q1 seasonality in security ECL and telecom.
